title: Are Heat Pumps Worth It in Oklahoma? Everything You Need to Know
summary: An Oklahoma HVAC dealer answers common heat pump questions: savings versus electric strips and propane, replacing a furnace, load calculation, refrigerant charge and cost.

assertions.quote: anybody that has Total Electric is going to drastically improve by having a actual heat pump as opposed to using electric heat strips
especially if you have propane you can definitely save quite a bit
they have actually taken heat pumps in Alaska and they don't have backup heat
you need to calculate what your heat load is going to be on that house

verdicts.note: Heating load calculations predicted Site 8's excessive auxiliary heat use from undersizing, and the report says auxiliary use should be minimized by proper sizing and controls.

assertions.quote: unless you're in that kind of situation where you're getting free gas I would say we can definitely save you money
in a heat pump it is very crucial that we have the correct charge on there

verdicts.note: Lab and field studies show refrigerant charge errors and mismatched coils cut heat pump capacity and efficiency, more so in heating.
Lab tests on a two-stage heat pump found individual over- and undercharge faults raised cooling energy 4-9%, with a 30% undercharge limiting capacity so the set point could not be held at peak.

assertions.quote: how much would it cost to put in a heat pump and that answer is going to be it depends

verdicts.note: Installed costs remain extremely variable even after corrections, driven by deferred maintenance, pricing strategies, market experience, integration with existing systems and local codes.
Edwards reports that heat pump costs vary substantially across households and regions (typically $5,000-$10,000 for air-source) with home size, efficiency, climate, labour and installer experience.

LBNL (642 heat pump installs, median $8,027): costs vary substantially by heat pump type (ground source nearly 3x others), and the main cost drivers were capacity, type, floor area, efficiency, climate zone, program and stories.
Invoice totals varied widely by region and install complexity; upgrade costs alone ranged from $3,258 to $18,400 excluding the equipment, with major duct work tied to big price jumps.
Heat pump equipment and installation costs vary widely in Canada, driven by limited suppliers in some regions and largely by brand, while gas systems vary less.

assertions.quote: the short answer to that can a heat pump replace a furnace yes

verdicts.note: Air-to-air heat pumps are reversible and provide air conditioning, which makes their incremental cost over a legacy furnace plus AC more favourable.
Edwards explains that heat pumps heat and, by reversing the refrigerant, cool, replacing the separate furnace and air conditioner of a conventional system.
Mass Save: air-source heat pumps extract outdoor heat in winter and reverse to cool in summer, and whole-home rebates go to homes using the heat pump as the sole source of heating and cooling.
At most sites a furnace was replaced by a single ducted cold-climate heat pump that then supplied both heating and cooling (median cooling COPs 3.4-5.4) with built-in resistance backup.
Heat pumps double as cooling, but a backup heating system may still be needed in parts of Canada during the coldest periods and insurers often require one, so the model adds backup in every city.
